title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Kung Pao Chicken is a classic Sichuan dish featuring tender diced chicken tossed with dried red chilies, fragrant Sichuan peppercorns, roasted peanuts, and scallions in a glossy sweet, savory, and tangy sauce. High-heat wok cooking creates an aromatic, smoky finish characteristic of professional restaurant-style preparation.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken Marinade
items: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs – 500 g (1 lb), diced into 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.title: For the Sauce
items: Cornstarch – 1 tsp, mixed with 2 tsp water

ingredients.title: For the Aromatics & Main Dish
items: Dried red chilies – 8–10 (facing heaven chilies preferred)
Scallions – 4, white and green parts separated
Roasted peanuts – ½ cup, unsalted and skinless
Neutral oil – 3 tbsp (peanut or grapeseed oil recommended)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Marinating the Chicken
steps: Place the diced chicken in a bowl.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, cornstarch, and sesame oil.
Mix thoroughly until evenly coated and let rest for 15–20 minutes.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Preparing the Sauce
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Chinkiang black vinegar, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Set the cornstarch slurry aside separately for thickening the sauce during the final stage.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Aromatic Oil Infusion
steps: Heat a wok over medium-high heat until just smoking.
Add the neutral oil, followed by dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns.
Stir-fry for 10–15 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn the chilies or peppercorns.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Stir-Frying the Chicken
steps: Add the marinated chicken to the wok.
Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until browned and nearly cooked through.
Push the chicken toward the sides of the wok.
Add garlic, ginger, and chopped scallion whites to the center and stir-fry briefly until aromatic.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Sauce & Finishing
steps: Pour the prepared sauce mixture into the wok.
Toss vigorously until the chicken is evenly coated.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook for 30–60 seconds until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze.
Add the roasted peanuts and scallion greens, tossing quickly to combine.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Serving
steps: Transfer the Kung Pao Chicken immediately to a heated serving plate.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice or hand-pulled noodles.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve traditionally with steamed jasmine rice.
Pair with hand-pulled noodles for a more substantial Sichuan-style meal.
Serve immediately while the sauce is glossy and the peanuts remain crisp.

chefTips: For a stronger Sichuan kick, leave the chili seeds intact; remove them for milder heat.
Roast peanuts fresh whenever possible for maximum aroma and crunch.
Cashews can be substituted for peanuts when a more delicate nutty texture is desired.
Use high heat and quick wok movements to develop wok hei and achieve a restaurant-quality finish.
Adjust the sugar and Chinkiang vinegar to achieve the preferred sweet-sour balance.
Add peanuts only at the end so they retain their characteristic crunch.
